**Observations:**
- **Image border.** Row 0 and the corner pixels carry only tiny weights (|w| about 0.03), which looks like untouched initialization noise. So those pixels are almost always zero in the training data.
- **Top rows are active.** From row 1 (inputs ~32–41, columns 4–13) the weights become large (0.15–0.26). Row 2 (inputs ~59–83) has strong weights (up to about 0.4–0.48) across most of the width, roughly columns 4–23.
- **Bottom rows are active.** Rows 24–26 (inputs ~680–750) also carry strong weights across a wide horizontal span, roughly columns 3–20. Some units are very strongly tuned there; for example, unit 5 reaches about 0.3–0.5 on rows 24–25.
- **Left and right edges.** In the middle rows, pixels near columns 0–3 and 24–27 still have non-trivial weights.
- **What the units seem to detect.** They respond to large-scale silhouettes rather than thin strokes. Some respond to broad top areas, some to the full width, some to a band across the bottom.
- **Output layer.** Every hidden unit feeds into several classes with weights of mixed sign. No obvious one-unit-per-class pattern stands out.

**Reasoning:**
- **MNIST is ruled out.** MNIST digits are size-normalized into a 20×20 box centred in the 28×28 frame. Rows 0–3 and 24–27 are therefore almost always blank, and their weights would stay near initialization. Here, rows 1–2 and 24–26 carry some of the largest weights in the network. The objects must fill nearly the entire frame, from the very top to the very bottom and across most of the width.
- **Fashion-MNIST fits this.** Its clothing images fill the frame. Shirts, pullovers and coats occupy the full top and width, with collars near rows 0–2. Trousers and dresses span top to bottom. Sneakers, sandals and ankle boots put their soles in a wide horizontal band at the bottom (rows 23–26), which matches the strong bottom-band units.
- **KMNIST is possible but less likely.** Its characters are also large, but they would not typically produce such a clean bottom-band "sole" detector or such broad top-wide blobs.

**Dataset:** Fashion-MNIST (Zalando's 28×28 grayscale clothing article images).

**Classes:**
- 0 T-shirt/top
- 1 Trouser
- 2 Pullover
- 3 Dress
- 4 Coat
- 5 Sandal
- 6 Shirt
- 7 Sneaker
- 8 Bag
- 9 Ankle boot

**Confidence:** 70%
